rules: earnings_per_share (and other per-share fundamentals) divided by $close is a known scale error: $close is dividend-adjusted, earnings_per_share is raw-share-count scale, so the ratio leaks future dividend info. This round's top accept (fitness 8.246) is this exact pattern and is likely inflated, not genuine alpha. Anchor per-share fundamental ratios on $open instead.

A single window-length change on an archived aggregator (e.g. TS_MEAN(x,5) vs archived TS_MEAN(x,10), TS_MAX($high,10) vs archived TS_MAX($high,21), TS_MEAN(x,21) vs archived TS_MEAN(x,63)) leaves the whole unchanged payload as one large shared subtree, so it gets rejected regardless of how far the window moved. 4 of this round's 20 rejects were this. Vary the payload (field or inner operator), not just the window, when reusing an archived idea.

Wrapping an already-archived field in a different smoothing operator does not decorrelate: RANK(TS_MEAN($roa,21)) hit rho=0.967 against RANK($roa), and EMA($dollar_volume,21) hit rho=0.996 against TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21). Treat TS_MEAN and EMA of the same field as functionally the same signal for the correlation gate.

Crossover fusions built on RANK($roa) as a parent keep landing at exactly 2 shared nodes and get rejected as not-a-fusion (3 rejects this round, paired with a zscore interaction, a high-low rank, and a sign-of-delta term). RANK($roa) is a 2-node subtree, so no donation from it can ever reach the required 3-node overlap. Use a larger archive member as the fusion parent.

Leverage-based factors failed the cheap screen twice this round (delta of leverage over 63 days at t=0.62, leverage zscore times return volatility at t=0.45). Leverage alone is weak signal in the 2000-2013 cheap window here; it needs a stronger co-factor or should be deprioritized for now.

For roe, level-vs-trend framing is weak (roe minus its 63-day EMA failed cheap screen at t=0.38) while change-volatility framing is strong (volatility of daily roe changes was accepted at fitness 2.184). Prefer second-moment/volatility constructions over deviation-from-trend for this field.

Bare intraday range ratios normalized by a rolling min or max keep falling just short of the cheap screen even at their best this round (high-low over low-minus-rolling-min at t=0.71, high-minus-rolling-max times a volume-delta zscore at t=0.91). This family needs a stronger secondary signal than a bare range ratio to clear the bar.

Two rejects this round were exact duplicates of earlier proposals in the same run (a 63-day roa delta, and a 21-day correlation of absolute return with volume). Check new candidates against this round's own proposal list, not just the archive, before submitting.
